## Discussion (2)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-08T23:44:59Z

**Lane escalation — issue #661 done-means RED surfaced a conflict with the issue's own premise. Requesting a ruling on one of the six keys before proceeding.**

RED is proven (exit 1, clauses a+b fail, controls c+d pass pre-fix by design). But clause (b) failed for a reason the issue did not anticipate, and reading WHY rather than banking the tally (round 18) turned up a contradiction:

```
FAIL  (b) the launcher start path threw before completing:
          Local clone mode prohibits EMBEDDING_WATCHDOG_RESTART_SCRIPT
```

**`EMBEDDING_WATCHDOG_RESTART_SCRIPT` cannot be honored in local-clone mode as the issue asks.**

- `src/local-clone-mode.ts:15` lists it in `PROHIBITED_PATH_KEYS`; lines 190-194 throw `Local clone mode prohibits ${key}` if it has any non-empty value. `src/local-clone-mode.test.ts:138-145` pins that prohibition with a passing test.
- In the deployed env file it is set **empty**: `/Volumes/ThunderBolt/open-brain-local/local-clone.env:17` reads `EMBEDDING_WATCHDOG_RESTART_SCRIPT=`. That is the documented clone-mode suppression form — `docs/local-clone-dogfood.md:147` shows exactly `EMBEDDING_WATCHDOG_RESTART_SCRIPT=`, the same shape as `QMD_PATH=`.
- It was announced as dropped only because `describeDroppedChildEnvironment` skips on `undefined`, not on empty string (`scripts/local-clone.ts:212`). An explicitly-empty key reads as "configured" to the reporter.

So for this key the issue's premise — "configured deliberately in the operator-owned env file; dropping it is the bug" — does not hold. It is deliberately *disabled*, and adding it to `CHILD_ENV_KEYS` would either pass an empty string to the child (harmless but pointless, `src/embedding.ts:140` treats empty as unset) or, if ever given a real path, hand the clone a prohibited capability the guard exists to refuse. The other five (`LOG_LEVEL=debug`, `LOG_MAX_BYTES=67108864`, `LOG_MAX_FILES=12`, `SERVICE_NAME=open-brain`, `OPENBRAIN_MCP_AUDIT_ENABLED=1`) are all genuinely configured with real values and match the issue exactly.

**Options, one decision:**

1. **Honor five, silence the sixth at the reporter.** Add the five real keys to `CHILD_ENV_KEYS`; teach `describeDroppedChildEnvironment` to skip empty-string values (an explicitly-empty key is a deliberate suppression, not a dropped configuration). Boot goes fully silent as clause (b) requires, the prohibition stays intact, and the announce mechanism stops reporting a class of false positives it will otherwise keep generating for `QMD_PATH`-style suppressions.
2. **Honor five, leave the sixth announced.** Same five, no reporter change. Boot stays noisy about one key forever, so clause (b) as the issue specifies it ("announcement goes SILENT, dropped count 0") cannot pass — the done-means would need rewording to "names only the prohibited-and-empty key."
3. **Honor all six as literally written.** Requires removing or narrowing the `PROHIBITED_PATH_KEYS` guard and deleting its test. I do not recommend this and would want it as its own issue with a security rationale; the guard is a clone-mode isolation boundary.

My read is **option 1** — it satisfies the issue's four-clause design as written, keeps the isolation guard, and fixes a reporter false-positive that is the same accept-and-ignore class the #659 thread is about. But this reverses part of ledger item 29.2's "all six" wording, so it is a flagged deviation and yours to rule on, not mine to take silently.

Lane is holding at RED with the worktree intact. No fix written yet.

### rodaddy — 2026-08-09T00:05:14Z

**Amended scope shipped in PR #663 — ruling 29.2a, recorded here so the issue matches what ships.**

This issue asked for six keys. Five are honored; the sixth is deliberately not, and the reporter that named it was fixed instead.

**Honored** (added to `CHILD_ENV_KEYS`, `scripts/local-clone.ts`):
`LOG_LEVEL`, `LOG_MAX_BYTES`, `LOG_MAX_FILES`, `OPENBRAIN_MCP_AUDIT_ENABLED`, `SERVICE_NAME`

**Not honored:** `EMBEDDING_WATCHDOG_RESTART_SCRIPT`. It is in `PROHIBITED_PATH_KEYS` (`src/local-clone-mode.ts:15`), refused with any non-empty value (lines 190-194), pinned by a passing test (`src/local-clone-mode.test.ts:138-145`). The launcher throws on it before the allowlist is consulted, so honoring it would hand the clone a capability its own isolation guard exists to refuse.

**Why it appeared in the boot line at all** — and this is the part worth keeping: the env file sets it EMPTY (`local-clone.env:17`), which `docs/local-clone-dogfood.md:147` documents as the suppression form, same shape as an explicit empty `QMD_PATH`. The #659 drop reporter skipped only on `undefined`, so a deliberately-DISABLED key was reported as dropped CONFIGURATION. The original "all six" text in this issue is that false positive, propagated into a ruling.

So `describeDroppedChildEnvironment` now reads three states: unset (not reported), set-empty (a deliberate off switch, not reported), set-valued (configured, reported if dropped). Not a new semantic — clone mode already requires an explicit empty `QMD_PATH` to suppress the production default (`src/local-clone-mode.ts:203-209`); the reporter now reads empty the same way the validator already does.

Announcing a drop stays the right mechanism. Announcing a deliberate suppression is the mirror defect: a false positive that teaches an operator the boot line is noise. This issue is the receipt for that cost.

Done-means: `scripts/done-means/661-launcher-honors-six-keys.sh` — 5 clauses, RED-first (3 failed pre-fix, 2 controls passed by design), GREEN after. Two real mutants killed; one equivalent mutant reported honestly in the PR rather than dressed up as a kill.
